_comments: The four seeded contract types (plan §7 / ERD §7). CONFIGURATION-AS-DATA in the narrow sense
that survived the rebuild: exactly ONE column carries a rule — RequiresExecutedDocument — and
it is read by the derived IsAwaitingDocument, never branched on by name.
v1 seeded six types with fourteen columns of billing defaults (term months, billing frequency,
escalation percents, renewal mode, coterm). All of it is gone: v2 does not bill, does not renew
on a schedule, and does not decide anything from a type beyond whether paper is expected. The
vocabulary changed too — MSA / Standard / Membership / Evergreen / Pilot described commercial
shapes; Order Form / SOW / Payment Link / Change Order describe what the DOCUMENT is, which is
what a tracking app can actually observe.
Fixed UUIDs so a re-push against a rebuilt database UPDATES these rows rather than creating a
second set. Deliberately a NEW block (3333…10xx) rather than reusing v1's 3333…000x: the rows
are not edits of the old ones, and a from-zero rebuild should not resurrect an MSA row as an

fields.Name: Order Form
fields.Description: The commercial document a customer signs to buy — the ordinary agreement. Sits beneath a Master Agreement whose provisions it incorporates by reference, which is why the Order Form carries the ContractTemplateID rather than the MA carrying anything about it.

fields.Name: Statement of Work
fields.Description: Scoped services with a defined end. Amith, 2026-08-18: SOWs have standard language but no versioned template — so an SOW contract may have no ContractTemplateID, and that is not a gap to fill. Paper is still expected.

fields.Name: Payment Link
fields.Description: The sub-$10k self-serve case: finance sends a HubSpot payment link that references the Master Agreement, and nobody signs anything. There is an implied contract, so it IS a contract — it has a ContractTemplateID and no document. This is the one type where RequiresExecutedDocument is false, and the reason that column exists at all.

fields.Name: Change Order
fields.Description: Amends an existing agreement rather than replacing it: signed paper of its own, its own dates, and a ParentContractID naming what it changes. A change order must name a parent (enforced in the server subclass, which needs the type join to know it is one) — the derived IsChangeOrder reads the FK, not this row.
